{{Navbar-Global Gas Infrastructure Tracker}}
'''Texas Gas Transmission Pipeline''' is an operating natural gas pipeline in the United States.<ref name=source1>[http://bit.ly/2esJPHG Texas Gas Transmission Pipeline,] Wikipedia, accessed January 2018</ref>

==Location==
The pipeline runs from the Louisiana Gulf coast up through Arkansas, Mississippi, Tennessee, and Kentucky, to supply gas to Illinois, Indiana, and Ohio.

==Background==

=== Main Line ===
Texas Gas Transmission is operated by Texas Gas Transmission, LLC, a subsidiary of Boardwalk Pipeline Partners<ref>[http://www.txgt.com/ Welcome To Texas Gas], Texas Gas Transmission, accessed January 2018</ref> The pipeline brings gas from the Gulf Coast and Fayetteville Shale supply areas to the Midwest and to off-system markets in the Northeast.<ref>[http://abarrelfull.wikidot.com/texas-gas-transmission-pipeline Texas Gas Transmission], A Barrel Full, accessed January 2018.</ref> It is a bidirectional interstate natural gas pipeline that transports natural gas from supply areas in Arkansas, Louisiana, Texas, Pennsylvania, Ohio, and West Virginia to markets throughout the Midwestern and South Central United States.<ref name=":0" />
===Clarksville Interconnection Pipeline===
The pipeline expansion would have been built in Kentucky and Tennessee, USA.<ref name="eia" /><ref name="ftmap">[https://www.fractracker.org/2020/02/national-energy-petrochemical-map/ National Energy and Petrochemical Map] , FracTracker, February 28, 2020</ref> U.S FERC approved the project proposal in October 2014.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://clarksvillenow.com/local/feds-approve-gas-pipeline-in-ky-tenn/|title=Feds approve gas pipeline in Ky., Tenn.|last=Smith|first=Chris|date=15 October, 2014|website=Clarksville Now|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=10 August, 2023}}</ref> Locals had raised environmental concerns regarding the project.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theleafchronicle.com/story/news/local/clarksville/2017/02/06/gas-pipeline-city-council-divided-authorizing-exercise-eminent-domain/97552470/|title=Gas Pipeline: City Council divided on authorizing exercise of eminent domain|work=The Leaf-Chronicle|access-date=2023-08-10|language=en-US}}</ref> According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration the project is considered shelved.<ref name=eia>[https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php Natural Gas Data, Pipeline Projects] Energy Information Agency, accessed July 21, 2020</ref> There hasn't been any update on the project since 2017, thus the status of the project is presumed cancelled.

=== Borealis Project ===
In April 2025, Texas Gas announced an open season for the Borealis Project, which would take Marcellus and Utica gas to demand centers across the main pipeline's service territory. This would involve the construction of a greenfield line from Lebanon, OH, to Clarington, OH. The project scope included other modifications to TGT facilities in Ohio to expand capacity south to the Gulf Coast.<ref name=":3" />
